parties: Logicap (Alta Capital Management), acquiring; Xander Investment Management (Singapore-based), divesting
headline: Logicap completes acquisition of warehousing assets from Xander Investment Management
sum: Alta Capital's logistics platform Logicap acquired 2.6 million sq. ft. of operational warehousing assets in Chennai (free trade zone) and Kolkata (Bagnan) from Singapore-based Xander for ~₹1,500 crore in the first tranche, with a planned second tranche of 1 million sq. ft. in Bhiwandi (Mumbai) valued at ~₹500 crore, positioning Logicap as India's third-largest warehousing operator.
implication: Cross-border real estate platform acquisition by inbound PE firm demonstrates institutional investor appetite for stabilised, fully-let Grade-A logistics assets in Tier-1 cities; free trade zone arbitrage (Chennai facility) exemplifies structuring nuance in logistics M&A; execution across two tranches with different geographies (port-centric vs. consumption-corridor focus) signals staged portfolio integration strategy.
detail: Logicap (founded 2022, part of Alta Capital established 2021 by former Blackstone executive Siddhartha Gupta) acquired 2.6 million sq. ft. of fully-occupied warehousing from Singapore-based Xander Investment Management for approximately ₹1,500 crore. The first tranche comprises a 1.9 million sq. ft. logistics park in Chennai's free trade zone (duty deferments and tax benefits) and a 700,000 sq. ft. facility in Bagnan, Kolkata, both operational and leased to blue-chip tenants (DHL Supply Chain, DB Schenker, Flipkart). A second tranche of 1 million sq. ft. in Bhiwandi (Mumbai) is planned. Total deal value estimated at approximately ₹2,000 crore. The sale marks Xander's exit from India's warehousing sector (entered 2019 with $250 million industrial venture). Logicap's portfolio post-acquisition reaches approximately 25 million sq. ft., behind Horizon Industrial Parks (60.5 million sq. ft.) and IndoSpace (58 million sq. ft.). The transaction reflects inbound investment and PE-backed platform consolidation in India's high-growth logistics real estate market.

framework.note: Governs formation, execution, and enforcement of asset purchase agreement; critical for validating consideration, conditions precedent, and remedies for breach.

framework.ref: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, § 3 et seq.
framework.note: Central to title transfer and registration; particularly § 53 (part performance) and § 54 (sale of immovable property); applicable to land/facility conveyance in Chennai FTZ and Kolkata/Bhiwandi sites.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, § 4 et seq.
framework.note: Central; governs inbound investment by Singapore-registered entity and cross-border payment; acquisition of immovable property in India by non-resident FPI requires RBI approval under Schedule I.

framework.ref: Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act, 2005, § 1 et seq., read with SEZ Rules, 2006
framework.note: Central for Chennai facility sited in free trade zone; governs eligibility of asset use, tax benefits, duty deferment regime, and transfer restrictions on SEZ-located facilities; amended 2019.

framework.ref: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (LARR) Act, 2013, § 1 et seq.
framework.note: Applicable if any component of facilities involved prior state land or rehabilitation; not directly triggered if purely private-to-private immovable asset sale, but relevant to due diligence on title provenance.

framework.ref: Tamil Nadu Non-Agricultural Land Act, 1969 (and Kolkata/West Bengal equivalents)
framework.note: State-level restrictions on non-agricultural land transfer; Chennai and Kolkata facilities may trigger pre-registration approval or consent requirements; amended 2019 (TN).
Applied during due diligence to ensure asset ownership is not benami; acquisition by Singapore entity requires proof of genuine beneficial interest and no circular routing.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, § 194L (TCS on property), § 50C (stamp duty component), § 47(vi) (exemption for share-for-share swap if applicable)
framework.note: TCS on acquisition; stamp duty compliance; amended 2024; critical for closing mechanics and tax efficiency structuring if any share exchange involved.

framework.ref: Warehousing Development Regulatory Authority (WDRA) Regulations (if applicable) and Ministry of Commerce & Industry guidelines on logistics infrastructure
framework.note: Sector-specific; determines eligibility for deemed export treatment, GST rates on ancillary services, customs clearance protocols for cross-docking operations within Chennai FTZ.

structure.consideration: First tranche: ~₹1,500 crore (cash) for 2.6 million sq. ft. in Chennai (1.9M sq ft in FTZ) and Kolkata/Bagnan (0.7M sq ft). Second tranche: ~₹500 crore (estimated) for 1 million sq. ft. in Bhiwandi (Mumbai). Total: ~₹2,000 crore.
conditions: Completion of legal due diligence on title and absence of encumbrances (fully operational, no litigation noted).
Tenant consents/waiver of change-of-control clauses in lease agreements with DHL Supply Chain, DB Schenker, Flipkart and other blue-chip occupants.
FEMA approval from RBI for inbound acquisition by Singapore entity (non-resident FPI).
State-level non-agricultural land transfer approvals/consent in Tamil Nadu (Chennai) and West Bengal (Kolkata), if required under local law.
Regulatory clearance (if any) under SEZ Act 2005 for Chennai free-trade-zone facility regarding asset use and transfer.
Satisfactory environmental and labour compliance audit; no pending litigation or regulatory violations.
Second tranche (Bhiwandi) conditional on market conditions and negotiation of land/development terms (planned, not yet closed).
approvals: RBI approval for inbound investment by foreign entity (Singapore-registered Xander Investment Management).
SEBI approval unlikely (unless structured as securities offering; typically asset purchase does not trigger SEBI).
State governments (Tamil Nadu, West Bengal) non-agricultural land transfer consent.
SEZ Authority (Chennai facility) confirmation of asset eligibility and compliance with FTZ regulations.
Tenant consents and lease amendment/waiver executed for change-of-control in facility occupancy.
structure.novel: Two-tranche structure (first tranche completed, second planned) allows staged de-risking and market-responsive expansion. Free-trade-zone arbitrage (Chennai facility) monetises customs duty deferment and tax benefits under SEZ Act as material deal driver. Fully-occupied operational asset acquisition (no development risk) differs from typical Logicap greenfield/brownfield development model; signals portfolio maturation and institutional de-risking. Cross-border (Singapore–India) acquisition by inbound PE firm (Alta Capital, founded 2021) demonstrates emerging institutional capital penetration in India's tier-1 logistics markets.

triggers.note: Inbound acquisition by non-resident FPI (Singapore entity) of immovable property in India; RBI approval mandatory.
Sale of immovable property (facilities and land); part-performance and registration with state authorities required.
Chennai facility sited in free trade zone; transfer and use restrictions; duty deferment implications.

triggers.law: State Land Laws (Tamil Nadu NALA 1969, West Bengal equivalents)
triggers.note: Non-agricultural land transfer consent/approval for facilities in Chennai and Kolkata.
TCS on immovable property acquisition and stamp duty implications for value determination.
